content:
Quick answer: If you disagree with a PIP refusal for fibromyalgia, check the date and reasons on your decision letter. In England and Wales you can usually ask for mandatory reconsideration within one month, by phone, letter or the official form. If you still disagree after reconsideration, you can appeal to an independent tribunal. No diagnosis or wording guarantees an award.

First check which decision and which benefits system apply

This guide concerns challenging a Personal Independence Payment decision, not diagnosing or treating fibromyalgia. PIP decisions concern specific daily living and mobility activities. A diagnosis can explain your symptoms, but it does not by itself establish the points for an award. See our PIP eligibility guide for the wider criteria.

The steps below describe England and Wales. Northern Ireland has a separate PIP disputes process. In Scotland, check the decision letter and Adult Disability Payment information; do not assume DWP's reconsideration and tribunal route applies to a Social Security Scotland decision.

Ask for mandatory reconsideration in time

GOV.UK says you can request reconsideration by phone, letter or the official form, using the contact details on your decision letter. The usual deadline is one month from the date on that letter. If you write, the request must arrive by the deadline. Keep a copy of what you send and a record of any phone call.

Do not assume you have to obtain a new specialist report before making contact. If the deadline is close, ask the benefits office how to submit your request and any further evidence. If it has already passed, contact the office promptly: GOV.UK allows late requests for a good reason, such as hospital admission or bereavement, but you must explain the delay. Acceptance is not automatic.

Explain the decision you disagree with, activity by activity

Start with the reasons in your letter. Identify the activity, what you think was missed or misunderstood, and a specific example. A useful explanation describes what happens when you try, whether you need help or an aid, how long it takes, and whether you can repeat it when needed.

The DWP assessment criteria require activities to be considered reliably: safely, to an acceptable standard, repeatedly and within a reasonable time. They also explain how fluctuating difficulties are considered over time. Describe better and worse days and how frequently each occurs. Do not present your worst day as every day, or leave out genuine difficulties because you managed once at an assessment.

Illustrative example, not wording to copy: Instead of only saying that fatigue makes cooking difficult, describe what happened during a recent attempt to prepare a simple meal, which part you could not complete, what help you needed, how often that happens and what occurred afterwards. Use your own facts, including occasions when you manage more easily.

Use evidence that relates to the disputed activities

Relevant evidence may include existing care plans, medical or therapy reports, and specific observations from someone who supports you. Explain how it relates to the decision rather than sending only a general description of fibromyalgia. GOV.UK asks you to explain which part of the decision is wrong and why, and to send additional evidence supporting those reasons.

A GP or therapist may be able to describe functional limitations, but neither a particular letter nor an occupational therapy report guarantees points. Ask what evidence you already have before paying for a new report: GOV.UK says you cannot claim back the cost of evidence you pay for. Send personal documents only through the official benefits or tribunal route, not in a public comment on this website.

If the reconsideration decision is still wrong

For England and Wales, GOV.UK's benefit appeal guidance says an appeal is free and normally must be made within one month of getting the mandatory reconsideration decision. The tribunal is independent of government. If an appeal is late, explain why; it might not be accepted. Follow the notice and the official appeal service rather than assuming the reconsideration request itself starts an appeal.

There is no reliable personal success percentage for your case. An overall tribunal statistic would not predict the outcome of a fibromyalgia claim with your particular evidence. Citizens Advice warns that challenging the amount or length of an existing award can lead DWP to look at the whole claim again, so payments could be reduced or stopped. Get individual advice about that risk before proceeding. Our PIP appeal guide gives a fuller step-by-step overview.

Should you challenge or make a new claim?

A challenge asks whether the decision you received was wrong. A new claim is a different process. If your needs have changed, or you are considering both routes, get individual welfare-rights advice promptly. Do not assume a fresh application replaces a challenge, protects its deadline or preserves the same potential payment period.

Where to get help

GOV.UK signposts Citizens Advice, Advicenow and local advisers for free help and advice. Ask the service what it can offer locally; advice does not necessarily include representation at a hearing. Keep your decision letter, notices, forms and evidence together so an adviser can see the dates and disputed points.

Before you close this page: note the decision date, the relevant deadline, the activities you dispute and the official contact route. This is general benefits information, not individual legal advice or a prediction of an award. Source-checked on 17 November 2026.
